objective: Test assumption A97 (the owner's reading 'Distance is the only form of information'): do the pairwise bond distances of a not-all-equal base, read from its allowed states, determine those states? Exhaustive census for n <= 6, sampled n = 7; unsigned, signed and full-bond-set variants. Serves G1 and G16. Challenges A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-17 (Successful; referee pending): read as the program's bond distance between pairs, distance is not the only form of information: it fails at four distinctions and at six leaves 96% of not-all-equal bases sharing their distances with another; signed ties and distances between sets do not repair it; each bond with the joint states it excludes determines every base through six and every sampled one at seven. A97 under challenge: its plain reading overturned; it survives if distance includes orientation.
stop_rule: One frozen census and its read-out; A97 status set; referee hand-off; report.
title: Is distance the only form of information: bond-distance tables of not-all-equal bases
